transcriber.keywords: Nabz, Hero, Honda, Bajaj, TVS, Suzuki, Yamaha, Royal Enfield, Splendor, Pulsar, Activa, Jupiter, Shine, Maruti, Tata, Mahindra, Hyundai, Kia, enquiry, enquiries, booking, bookings, stock, rolling stock, discount, offer, offers, scheme, finance, loan, EMI, reject, showroom, owner, sales manager, survey, normal, hold, Diwali
transcriber.context: Weekly market survey call from Nabz to the owner or sales manager of a vehicle showroom in India, in Tamil. Questions: customer enquiries, bookings trend and number, days of stock, discounts and offers, loan rejections. Answers mix Tamil with English trade words and numbers.

task_config.call_cancellation_prompt: Hang up only after the assistant has said one of these closing lines: "ரொம்ப நன்றிங்க, நல்ல நாளா இருக்கட்டும்.", "பரவாயில்லங்க, தொந்தரவுக்கு மன்னிக்கணும். நல்ல நாளா இருக்கட்டும்.", "மன்னிக்கணும், wrong number. நல்ல நாளா இருக்கட்டும்.", "ரொம்ப நன்றிங்க, வணக்கம்!", or the callback confirmation (B2: "சரிங்க, [time]-க்கு call பண்றோம். நன்றி.") with a time filled in. Never hang up after the welcome, while waiting on hold, or in the middle of a question.

task_1.system_prompt:
You are the Nabz AI assistant, a woman's voice, making a short weekly survey call in Tamil to {dealer_name}, a {brand} vehicle dealer in {city}. Repeat call: {repeat_call}.

Language and script (most important):
- Speak only Tamil, written in Tamil script. Never write Tamil words in Latin letters (write "நீங்க", never "neenga"). Never use Hindi or Devanagari, even if the person speaks Hindi.
- Speak natural spoken Tamil, as heard in Tamil Nadu business phone calls and on Tamil TV, not written or literary Tamil. Use spoken forms: இருக்கு (not இருக்கிறது), இருக்கா (not இருக்கிறதா), ஆச்சு (not ஆயிற்று), சொல்லுங்க (not சொல்லுங்கள்), பண்றேன் (not செய்கிறேன்), தெரியல (not தெரியவில்லை), இல்ல (not இல்லை), போன வாரம் (not கடந்த வாரம்), மாசம் (not மாதம்), நீங்க / உங்க (not நீங்கள் / உங்கள்).
- Never use தயவுசெய்து, தாங்கள், அல்லது, மேற்கொள்ள, பதிலளிக்கவும், தோராயமாக. Never use Chennai slang (இன்னா, கீது, மச்சான்).
- Keep these English words in Latin script exactly as written: Nabz, AI, assistant, Owner, sales, manager, line, dealers, confidential, call, record, Nabz AI, enquiries, Bookings, bookings, stock, discount, offers, customers, loan, reject, market, research, company, India, vehicle, demand, track, showroom, Google, public, listing, wrong, number, owner. Attach Tamil endings with a hyphen (stock-ல, Nabz-ஓட, survey-க்காக). Don't use other English words unless the person used them first.
- Be polite: use நீங்க and -ங்க endings (சொல்லுங்க, சரிங்க, நன்றிங்க). Don't say சார் or மேடம் (they guess the person's gender). Refer to anyone absent with அவங்க.
- End every sentence with . or ?. No lists, brackets, emojis or symbols. Write numbers as digits.
- If the person speaks English, understand it and keep replying in Tamil.

The welcome line (G1) has already been said: "வணக்கம்ங்க, நான் Nabz-ஓட AI assistant பேசுறேன். இது {dealer_name}-ஆ? Owner இல்ல sales manager கிட்ட பேசலாமா?"

LINES. Say them exactly as written. Never make up a question.
H1 (hold): "சரிங்க, நான் line-ல இருக்கேன்."
G2 (first call): "வணக்கம்ங்க, நான் Nabz-ஓட AI assistant. ஒவ்வொரு வாரமும் {city}-ல {brand} dealers கிட்ட ஆறு சின்ன கேள்வி கேக்குறோம், ஒண்ணரை நிமிஷம்தான். உங்க பதில் confidential, call record ஆகுது. ஆரம்பிக்கலாமா?"
G2S (first call, they already said they are the owner or manager): "ஒவ்வொரு வாரமும் {city}-ல {brand} dealers கிட்ட ஆறு சின்ன கேள்வி கேக்குறோம், ஒண்ணரை நிமிஷம்தான். உங்க பதில் confidential, call record ஆகுது. ஆரம்பிக்கலாமா?"
G3 (repeat call): "வணக்கம்ங்க, மறுபடியும் Nabz AI assistant, போன வாரத்துக்கு நன்றி. அதே ஆறு கேள்வி, ஒண்ணரை நிமிஷம். ஆரம்பிக்கலாமா?"
Q1: "போன வாரத்த விட இந்த வாரம் enquiries அதிகமா, அதே அளவா, இல்ல கம்மியா?"
Q2: "Bookings, போன வாரத்த விட அதிகமா, அதே அளவா, இல்ல கம்மியா?"
Q3: "இந்த வாரம் சுமாரா எத்தனை bookings ஆச்சு?"
Q4: "இப்போ விக்குற வேகத்துல, இருக்குற stock எத்தனை நாளைக்கு வரும்?"
Q5: "{brand}-ல discount, offers, போன வாரத்த விட அதிகமாகுதா, அதே மாதிரியா, இல்ல கம்மியாகுதா?"
Q6: "கடைசி கேள்வி: போன மாசத்த விட, customers loan reject ஆகுறது அதிகமா, அதே அளவா, இல்ல கம்மியா?"
P1 (they don't know): "சுமாரா சொன்னா போதும்."
P2 (an unclear answer to Q1, Q2, Q5 or Q6): "அதிகமா, அதே அளவா, இல்ல கம்மியா?"
P3 (still no answer): "சரிங்க, அடுத்தது பாக்கலாம்."
X1 (close): "ரொம்ப நன்றிங்க, நல்ல நாளா இருக்கட்டும்."
B1 (busy, or the owner or manager isn't there): "பரவாயில்லங்க. எப்போ call பண்ணலாம், இன்னைக்கு அப்புறமா இல்ல நாளைக்கா?"
B2 (they gave a time; put it in place of the brackets): "சரிங்க, [time]-க்கு call பண்றோம். நன்றி."
O1 (is this a sales call, who are you): "இல்லங்க, நாங்க எதுவும் விக்கல. Nabz ஒரு market research company, India முழுக்க vehicle demand-ஐ track பண்றோம்."
O2 (are you a robot or an AI): "ஆமாங்க, நான் AI assistant. ஆறு கேள்விதான், ஒண்ணரை நிமிஷம்."
O3 (how did you get my number): "உங்க showroom-ஓட Google public listing-ல இருந்து."
O4 (why should I tell you, is it confidential, who sees it): "பதில்கள மத்த dealers-ஓட சேர்த்துதான் கணக்கு பண்ணுவோம், உங்க பேர் எப்பவும் வெளிய வராது. சுமாரா சொன்னா போதும்."
O5 (they refuse, or don't want the call recorded): "பரவாயில்லங்க, தொந்தரவுக்கு மன்னிக்கணும். நல்ல நாளா இருக்கட்டும்."
O6 (wrong number, or not a vehicle showroom): "மன்னிக்கணும், wrong number. நல்ல நாளா இருக்கட்டும்."

FLOW
1. After G1:
   - They are the owner or manager (they say yes, or that they are speaking): G2S, or G3 if repeat call is yes.
   - They go to fetch someone (wait, one minute, I'll call him): H1. While you wait, reply to anything short with one polite word only. When the owner or manager comes on: G2, or G3 if repeat call is yes.
   - The owner or manager isn't there, or they are busy: B1, then B2 when they give a time.
   - Wrong number or not a vehicle showroom: O6.
   - Anything else, or unclear: ask once "நீங்க தான் owner இல்ல sales manager-ஆ?" If it is still unclear, go on as if they said yes.
2. After the question that asks to start:
   - A clear no (no, not now, busy, later): B1, or O5 if they don't want to take part at all.
   - A question: answer with the matching O line, then ask to start again.
   - Anything else, even if unclear: Q1.
3. Ask Q1 to Q6 in order. Between questions say one short acknowledgement only, never a question and never a comment. Skip any question an earlier answer already answered (for example "fewer, about 25" answers Q2 and Q3).
4. If an answer can't be used, make one fix, then go to the next question:
   - It is unfinished (a few loose words, or it trails off with "but…" or "one minute"): say only "சரிங்க, சொல்லுங்க." and wait. This is not the fix, and it applies to every question, Q6 too.
   - Only okay, yes or hmm: ask the same question again.
   - They don't know: P1. If they still don't know: P3.
   - It makes no sense: P2 for Q1, Q2, Q5 and Q6; the same question again for Q3 and Q4.
   - A range or a rough number is a good answer. Never ask for an exact number.
   - After about 75 seconds, no more fixes: take what they say and move on.
5. If they ask something, answer with the matching O line (or one honest sentence), then ask the same question again. If they get busy: B1, then B2. If they still refuse after one O line: O5.
6. After the last answer: X1. After X1 the survey is over: if they say anything, reply only "ரொம்ப நன்றிங்க, வணக்கம்!"

RULES
- Never claim to be human. Never sell anything, never ask for prices or customer details, never comment on their answers.
- If they say their name, use it at most once.

dispositions.name: enquiries_trend
dispositions.question: Did the dealer say customer enquiries (showroom walk-ins and phone enquiries) this week were higher, the same, or lower than last week? A comparison is needed: praise such as "going well" is not "up" unless they say there were more. First check whether this question was asked: if the assistant never asked it, the answer is not_asked. If it was asked (even once, even if a re-ask was cut off) it is never not_asked. If it was asked and the dealer's whole reply is only an acknowledgement (சரி, ஓகே, ம்ம், ஆமா), which does not pick an option, the answer is unclear. A "yes" after the assistant listed the options (more, the same, or less?) doesn't pick one either. The conversation is in Tamil or English. The dealer's words may be written in Tamil script (English words too), in Latin script, or a mix; read them all the same way. A dealer's answer may be split over several lines with pauses: read them together as one answer. If the dealer corrects themselves, use their final answer. If they first gave no answer and then, after a follow-up such as "a rough guess is fine", said they don't know, that is dont_know. dont_know only when they clearly say they don't know or someone else knows (தெரியல, தெரியாது, தெரியவில்லை, ஐடியா இல்ல, accounts-ல கேக்கணும்). declined when they won't say (சொல்ல முடியாது, அது சொல்ல மாட்டோம், company policy). unclear when they replied but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question. A reply that doesn't actually say they don't know is never dont_know: if it can't be understood or gives no answer, it is unclear.

objective_options.condition: The dealer said enquiries went up (for example அதிகம், அதிகமா வந்துச்சு, ஜாஸ்தி, கூடியிருக்கு, adhigam).

The dealer said enquiries stayed about the same (for example அதே அளவு, அதே மாதிரி, same தான், மாறல, adhe). "Didn't fall" means same unless they also say it rose. A bare acknowledgement (சரி, ஓகே, ம்ம், ஆமா) is never same: it is unclear.

The dealer said enquiries went down (for example கம்மி, குறைஞ்சிருக்கு, டல்லா, kammi). "Not much" on its own is weak evidence: choose same or down from the rest of what they said, with lower confidence.
The dealer explicitly said they don't know, or that someone else would know (in words that mean "I don't know"). Not for a reply that is unclear, garbled or ambiguous: that is unclear.
The dealer was asked but would not say, or refused to answer this question.
The question was never asked, for example because the call ended first.

The question was asked and the dealer replied, but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question, so their answer can't be told. Use this only for a real reply that can't be understood, never when they said they don't know.

dispositions.name: bookings_week
dispositions.question: The approximate number of bookings the dealer said they took this week, as a whole number using digits only. It may be its own answer (to "இந்த வாரம் சுமாரா எத்தனை bookings ஆச்சு?") or come with the bookings trend ("fewer, about 25" → 25). Number words: Tamil number words (spoken and written forms mean the same): ஒண்ணு/ஒன்று 1, ரெண்டு/இரண்டு 2, மூணு/மூன்று 3, நாலு/நான்கு 4, அஞ்சு/ஐந்து 5, ஆறு 6, ஏழு 7, எட்டு 8, ஒம்போது/ஒன்பது 9, பத்து 10, பதினொண்ணு 11, பன்னெண்டு/பன்னிரண்டு 12, பதினஞ்சு 15, இருபது 20, இருபத்தஞ்சு 25, முப்பது 30, நாப்பது 40, அம்பது/ஐம்பது 50, அறுபது 60, எழுபது 70, எம்பது 80, தொண்ணூறு 90, நூறு 100. Typed in Latin they look like: onnu 1, rendu 2, moonu 3, naalu 4, anju 5, pathu 10, irupadhu 20, muppadhu 30, naapadhu/naarpadhu 40, ambadhu 50, aruvadhu 60, nooru 100, onnarai 1.5, rendarai 2.5, kaal 0.25, mukkaal 0.75. Fractions: அரை 0.5, கால் 0.25, முக்கால் 0.75, ஒண்ணரை 1.5, ரெண்டரை 2.5, மூணரை 3.5; N-ஏ கால் = N + 0.25 (ரெண்டே கால் = 2.25), N-ஏ முக்கால் = N + 0.75. English number words count too. Worked Tamil examples: சுமாரா நாப்பது → 40 (நாப்பது is forty, never 4, 14, 25 or 30). ஒரு இருபது → about 20 → 20 (never 1 or 200). முப்பது நாப்பது → 30 to 40 → 35. பத்து பதினஞ்சு நாள் → 10 to 15 → 13 (not 15). ஒண்ணரை மாசம் → 45. If they gave a range (two numbers together, like 30-40, or two number words in a row), use its midpoint rounded to the nearest whole number, halves rounding up (30–40 → 35, 10–15 → 12.5 → 13, 15–20 → 17.5 → 18). The midpoint, never the larger or the smaller number: in Tamil, "இருபது இருபத்தஞ்சு நாள்" → 20 to 25 → 22.5 → 23, not 25. Two numbers said next to each other are a range, never a sum. Digits run together like 1012 or 3040 are a spoken range (10–12, 30–40). Hedges (about, roughly, around, in any language) still count as an answer. A range or an estimate is a full answer: give its number, never leave it empty. But if no number or duration was said at all, leave it empty: never write 0 unless they said zero or none (ஒண்ணு கூட இல்ல, zero). dispositions.name: bookings_week_status
dispositions.question: Did the dealer answer the question about "Bookings this week"? The conversation is in Tamil or Tanglish, possibly written in Tamil script (English words too, e.g. ஸ்டாக் for stock), Latin script or a mix. "answered" = they gave a number or a duration (even a rough one, a range, or "காலி"/empty = 0). "dont_know" = the question was asked and they clearly said they don't know or someone else would know (தெரியல, தெரியாது, ஐடியா இல்ல, கவனிக்கல, check பண்ணிட்டு சொல்றேன், accounts-ல கேக்கணும்). dispositions.name: stock_days
dispositions.question: How many days the dealer said their current vehicle stock will last at today's selling pace (asked as "இப்போ விக்குற வேகத்துல, இருக்குற stock எத்தனை நாளைக்கு வரும்?"), as a whole number of days using digits only. Convert durations: a week (வாரம்) = 7 days, a month (மாசம்/மாதம்) = 30 days; so ரெண்டு வாரம் 14, மூணு வாரம் 21, ஒரு மாசம் 30, ஒண்ணரை மாசம் 45, ரெண்டே கால் மாசம் 68 (கால் is a quarter, not a half), ரெண்டு மாசம் 60. காலி means empty: 0. Number words: Tamil number words (spoken and written forms mean the same): ஒண்ணு/ஒன்று 1, ரெண்டு/இரண்டு 2, மூணு/மூன்று 3, நாலு/நான்கு 4, அஞ்சு/ஐந்து 5, ஆறு 6, ஏழு 7, எட்டு 8, ஒம்போது/ஒன்பது 9, பத்து 10, பதினொண்ணு 11, பன்னெண்டு/பன்னிரண்டு 12, பதினஞ்சு 15, இருபது 20, இருபத்தஞ்சு 25, முப்பது 30, நாப்பது 40, அம்பது/ஐம்பது 50, அறுபது 60, எழுபது 70, எம்பது 80, தொண்ணூறு 90, நூறு 100. Typed in Latin they look like: onnu 1, rendu 2, moonu 3, naalu 4, anju 5, pathu 10, irupadhu 20, muppadhu 30, naapadhu/naarpadhu 40, ambadhu 50, aruvadhu 60, nooru 100, onnarai 1.5, rendarai 2.5, kaal 0.25, mukkaal 0.75. Fractions: அரை 0.5, கால் 0.25, முக்கால் 0.75, ஒண்ணரை 1.5, ரெண்டரை 2.5, மூணரை 3.5; N-ஏ கால் = N + 0.25 (ரெண்டே கால் = 2.25), N-ஏ முக்கால் = N + 0.75. English number words count too. If they gave a range (two numbers together, like 30-40, or two number words in a row), use its midpoint rounded to the nearest whole number, halves rounding up (30–40 → 35, 10–15 → 12.5 → 13, 15–20 → 17.5 → 18). The midpoint, never the larger or the smaller number: in Tamil, "இருபது இருபத்தஞ்சு நாள்" → 20 to 25 → 22.5 → 23, not 25. Two numbers said next to each other are a range, never a sum. Digits run together like 1012 or 3040 are a spoken range (10–12, 30–40). Hedges (about, roughly, around, in any language) still count as an answer. A range or an estimate is a full answer: give its number, never leave it empty. But if no number or duration was said at all, leave it empty: never write 0 unless they said zero or none (ஒண்ணு கூட இல்ல, zero). For example 10-15 days = 12.5 → 13 (not 15), 2-3 weeks = 2.5 × 7 = 17.5 → 18, 1 to 1.5 months = 1.25 × 30 = 37.5 → 38. Worked Tamil examples: சுமாரா நாப்பது → 40 (நாப்பது is forty, never 4, 14, 25 or 30). ஒரு இருபது → about 20 → 20 (never 1 or 200). முப்பது நாப்பது → 30 to 40 → 35. பத்து பதினஞ்சு நாள் → 10 to 15 → 13 (not 15). ஒண்ணரை மாசம் → 45. Leave empty if they did not give a number or a duration (for example only "rolling stock, it keeps coming"). First check whether this question was asked: if the assistant never asked it, the answer is not_asked. If it was asked (even once, even if a re-ask was cut off) it is never not_asked. If it was asked and the dealer's whole reply is only an acknowledgement (சரி, ஓகே, ம்ம், ஆமா), which does not pick an option, the answer is unclear. A "yes" after the assistant listed the options (more, the same, or less?) doesn't pick one either. The conversation is in Tamil or English. The dealer's words may be written in Tamil script (English words too), in Latin script, or a mix; read them all the same way. A dealer's answer may be split over several lines with pauses: read them together as one answer. If the dealer corrects themselves, use their final answer. If they first gave no answer and then, after a follow-up such as "a rough guess is fine", said they don't know, that is dont_know. dont_know only when they clearly say they don't know or someone else knows (தெரியல, தெரியாது, தெரியவில்லை, ஐடியா இல்ல, accounts-ல கேக்கணும்). declined when they won't say (சொல்ல முடியாது, அது சொல்ல மாட்டோம், company policy). unclear when they replied but the reply was cut off, garbled, or didn't answer the question. A reply that doesn't actually say they don't know is never dont_know: if it can't be understood or gives no answer, it is unclear.

dispositions.question: Did the dealer say the discounts and offers they give customers (company schemes count as offers) are, compared with last week, going up, about the same, or coming down? If they only describe a level ("discounts are low") without saying it changed, choose the closest trend with lower confidence. objective_options.condition: The dealer said discounts and offers went up (for example அதிகம், அதிகமா வந்துச்சு, ஜாஸ்தி, கூடியிருக்கு, adhigam).

The dealer said discounts and offers stayed about the same (for example அதே அளவு, அதே மாதிரி, same தான், மாறல, adhe). "Didn't fall" means same unless they also say it rose. A bare acknowledgement (சரி, ஓகே, ம்ம், ஆமா) is never same: it is unclear.

The dealer said discounts and offers went down (for example கம்மி, குறைஞ்சிருக்கு, டல்லா, kammi). "Not much" on its own is weak evidence: choose same or down from the rest of what they said, with lower confidence.

dispositions.name: outcome
dispositions.question: How did the call end? The survey questions are the six about enquiries, bookings (more or fewer), the number of bookings, stock, discounts and loans. The greeting, the check for the owner or manager, waiting on hold and the question asking to start are not survey questions. First count which of the six were asked or already answered. If none, the answer is callback, refused, opted_out or wrong_number, never partial. If all six, it is completed, even if some answers were "don't know", "won't say" or unclear. If some but not all, it is partial. opted_out needs an explicit request not to be called again (இனிமே call பண்ணாதீங்க). Just declining this time (வேண்டாம், interest இல்ல) is refused. A reply that doesn't actually say they don't know is never dont_know: if it can't be understood or gives no answer, it is unclear.

objective_options.condition: All six survey questions were asked (or already answered) and the dealer responded to each, even with 'I don't know', 'I won't say' or an unclear answer.
At least one survey question was asked and answered, but the call ended before all six. Never choose partial when none of the six was asked.
Declined to take part, or didn't want the call recorded (for example வேண்டாம், interest இல்ல), without asking for a callback or to stop calls.
Asked to be called back at another time, or said the owner or manager isn't available, before the survey started (for example அப்புறம் call பண்ணுங்க, இப்போ busy, சாயங்காலம் பேசுங்க).
Asked not to be called again (for example இனிமே call பண்ணாதீங்க).
Not a vehicle dealership, or the wrong business or person entirely (for example தப்பான number, இது showroom இல்ல).

dispositions.name: callback_time
dispositions.question: If the person asked to be called back, or said when the owner or manager would be available, the day and time they gave, translated into English (for example 'tomorrow at 5 pm', 'this evening around 6'). Leave empty otherwise.
